newsitem.title: USA: Property Claim Services sees $980 mln in Q2 losses.
newsitem.headline: Property Claim Services sees $980 mln in Q2 losses.

text.p: Property Claim Services said Thursday it estimated $980 million in insured property losses from catastrophes during the second quarter of 1997, the lowest figure on losses in a second quarter since 1989.
A division of American Insurance Services Group Inc, Property Claims Services is an industry group that tracks insurance losses.
PCS identified nine catastrophes in its summary of insured property losses from catastrophes.
The catastrophe loss total for the first six months of 1997 is estimated at $1.84 billion from 17 catastrophes.

The division said the events causing the most damage during the quarter were the flooding in North Dakota at $225 million; the April wind, hail and rain storms in the upper mid-west at $160 million; and the late May storms in the southern tier of states at $140 million.
Gary Kerney, assistant vice president, said "The past quarter was one of the lightest in terms of insured property loss from catastrophes, over the past few years.
Historically, he said, most claim activity in the second quarter results from thunderstorms.
